your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: Vermont Avenue is cheap at $100 and extremely valuable early-game. Buying immediately signals aggressive play and starts the race for monopolies. Light blue properties are essential stepping stones. Cash impact is minimal (only 6.7% of bank). No reason to auction when this is one of the board's best early deals.

Vermont Avenue is locked in. No beneficial trades exist at this stage (opponents have no properties), and mortgaging my only holding would be irrational with $1,300 cash remaining. End turn to let the game progress and observe opponent behavior before the next acquisition phase.

Early acquisition is critical. $140 for a utility property in the pink set is solid. Cash position remains healthy at $1,260. Better to own it than let opponents bid it down in auction. Maintaining aggressive acquisition strategy from turn 1.

End turn. Vermont + States gives me optionality on two separate monopolies (light blue or pink). Early trading would lock me in prematurely. Cash ($1,260) is best spent on future acquisitions like St. Charles, Virginia, or Connecticut. No rush - positions are strong relative to opposition.

B&O Railroad acquisition: $200 leaves me at $1,060 cash. Single railroad generates $25 rent baseline. More importantly, denies opponents the chance to monopolize railroads. Early game cash is abundant—this is the right time to spend it on assets. Consistent with aggressive acquisition strategy (Vermont, States). Railroads typically become secondary income stream by mid-game, so securing one early is sound.
